result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick 7 measures, give a reason for each of the 7 left off, and cover both service and money. A is stronger on the misleading-measure item: it says to count only active cards for cardholders and to phase the budget plan by month so lumpy costs don't look like overspending. B never caveats inactive cards in its cardholder share. A also explains why each comparison was chosen, while B mostly gives that reasoning in its design notes. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a well-sized set of 7, give each measure a sensible comparison basis and cover both service and money. B does more on measures that can mislead: it counts only cardholders active in the last 2–3 years so dead cards don't inflate the total, and it compares spending to a month-by-month plan so lumpy costs don't look like overspending. A's caveats are limited to seasonality and cost-per-visit noise.
